text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak to head a ministerial meeting within days to follow up several national mega-projects. Two cement factories to be set up in Kharga oasis. Thirty million pounds ($8.8 million) for the Dakhla and East Oweinat airports. Two tourist villages and a hotel to be set up in the New Valley.

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright says the Egyptian role is the most active role in the Middle East peace process. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says: Albright's comments are a good basis to push forward the peace process.
- Arab tourism ministers demand a strategy to protect the touristic heritage.
- Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi says Egypt has a leading role in maintaining the security of the African continent.
- Egyptian authorities are taking necessary steps to bring back 45 ancient statues and other antiquities which were illegally taken away.

- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat says: We have foiled suicide attempts against Israel. U.S. President Bill Clinton says: Israel must show willingness and start taking action rather than just talking. London: The status of Jerusalem cannot be decided before the final status talks. Tokyo: American bias towards Israel made the Middle East peace process flag.
- Moussa says Egypt is monitoring the situation in northern Iraq.
- Construction work on Toshka's infrastructure is going quickly.
- Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif says the government is keen to support the freedom of the press.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri met Egyptian swimming medalist Rania Elwani and the youth football squad.
